# Charter of Fundamental Rights — Structure, Scope and Restriction Test

Curated static reference for the `eu-legislative` skills (`treaty-check`,
`impact-assessment`, `legislative-proposal`, `isc-contributor`,
`fundamental-rights-assessor`) and `eu-competition` (`lawyer-legal-service`).
The Charter has the same legal value as the Treaties (Art. 6(1) TEU).

Cite as: `(Charter, Art. X — EUR-Lex 12012P) [EUR-Lex — verify current version]`.

Legal sources:
- Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, OJ C 326, 26.10.2012
  `[EUR-Lex — verify current version]`
- Explanations relating to the Charter, OJ C 303, 14.12.2007 — interpretive
  authority under Art. 52(7) `[EUR-Lex — verify current version]`
- Art. 6 TEU; Protocol No 30 (Poland; formerly UK) `[EUR-Lex — verify current version]`

---

## Structure — the six substantive Titles + horizontal provisions

| Title | Articles | Rights most engaged by legislation |
|---|---|---|
| I — Dignity | 1–5 | Human dignity (1), integrity of the person (3), prohibition of torture (4), slavery/forced labour and trafficking (5) |
| II — Freedoms | 6–19 | Liberty (6), **private and family life (7)**, **protection of personal data (8)**, thought/religion (10), **expression and information (11)**, assembly/association (12), arts and sciences (13), education (14), **occupation and right to work (15)**, **freedom to conduct a business (16)**, **property incl. IP (17)**, asylum (18), removal protection (19) |
| III — Equality | 20–26 | **Equality before the law (20)**, **non-discrimination (21)**, cultural/religious/linguistic diversity (22), gender equality (23), rights of the child (24), elderly (25), persons with disabilities (26) |
| IV — Solidarity | 27–38 | Workers' information/consultation (27), collective bargaining and action (28), fair and just working conditions (31), social security (34), health care (35), **environmental protection (37)**, **consumer protection (38)** |
| V — Citizens' rights | 39–46 | Vote/stand in EP and municipal elections (39–40), **good administration (41)**, access to documents (42), Ombudsman (43), petition (44), movement and residence (45), diplomatic protection (46) |
| VI — Justice | 47–50 | **Effective remedy and fair trial (47)**, presumption of innocence and rights of defence (48), legality and proportionality of penalties (49), ne bis in idem (50) |
| VII — Horizontal | 51–54 | Scope, restriction test, level of protection, abuse of rights — see below |

## Art. 51 — Scope (who is bound)

- Addressed to the **Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies** (with
  due regard for subsidiarity) and to the **Member States only when they are
  implementing Union law** (C-617/10 *Åkerberg Fransson*: "implementing" =
  acting within the scope of Union law) `[CJEU — verify Curia reference]`.
- The Charter **does not extend Union competences** (Art. 51(2)) — a proposal
  cannot take the Charter as its legal basis.
- Practical consequence for drafting: every Commission act must be
  Charter-compliant in full; Member State implementation measures and
  discretionary choices left by a directive are also within Charter scope.

## Art. 52(1) — the restriction (limitation) test

Any limitation on a Charter right must cumulatively satisfy **all** of:

1. **Provided for by law** — a clear, precise, foreseeable legal rule (the act
   itself must define the limitation's scope; no blank delegations).
2. **Respect the essence** of the right — the core may never be extinguished
   (C-362/14 *Schrems I*: access to content of communications breached the
   essence of Art. 7) `[CJEU — verify Curia reference]`.
3. **Genuinely meet** objectives of general interest recognised by the Union
   **or** the need to protect the rights and freedoms of others.
4. **Proportionality** — suitable, **necessary** (no less restrictive equally
   effective measure: C-293/12 *Digital Rights Ireland* — blanket data
   retention failed necessity), and proportionate stricto sensu
   `[CJEU — verify Curia reference]`.

Document each step in the IA/explanatory memorandum for every right engaged —
asserting "the measure is proportionate" without the four-step analysis is the
standard RSB and Legal Service objection.

## Other horizontal rules (Arts. 52(2)–54)

| Provision | Rule |
|---|---|
| 52(2) | Charter rights based on the Treaties are exercised under the conditions and limits the Treaties define |
| 52(3) | Rights corresponding to ECHR rights have **at least** the ECHR meaning and scope (Union law may protect more) |
| 52(4) | Rights from common constitutional traditions are interpreted in harmony with them |
| 52(5) | **Principles** (vs rights) are judicially cognisable only via implementing acts (C-176/12 *AMS*: Art. 27 not directly invocable between private parties) `[CJEU — verify Curia reference]` |
| 52(7) | The **Explanations** "shall be given due regard" — cite them in the rights analysis |
| 53 | Level-of-protection clause — but national standards cannot defeat the primacy, unity and effectiveness of Union law (C-399/11 *Melloni*) `[CJEU — verify Curia reference]` |
| 54 | Prohibition of abuse of rights |

Protocol No 30 (Poland) clarifies justiciability, in particular for Title IV,
but does not amount to an opt-out (C-411/10 *N.S.*, para. 119)
`[CJEU — verify Curia reference]`.

## Standard preamble recital (legislative drafting)

> This Regulation respects the fundamental rights and observes the principles
> recognised in particular by the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the
> European Union, notably [Articles X, Y and Z]. It should be implemented in
> accordance with those rights and principles.

Name the specific articles actually engaged — a generic recital with no
article numbers signals that no rights analysis was done.

## Rights-engagement screening (IA Step / treaty-check)

Quick screen for the rights most commonly engaged by instrument type
`[model knowledge — verify against the Explanations]`:

| Measure type | Check first |
|---|---|
| Any processing of personal data | Arts. 7, 8 (+ alignment with GDPR/EUDPR) |
| Enforcement, inspection, sanction powers | Arts. 41, 47, 48, 49, 50; legal professional privilege (Art. 7) |
| Market access, licensing, prohibitions | Arts. 15, 16, 17 (incl. 17(2) IP) |
| Platform/content/media rules | Arts. 11, 8, 16; media freedom and pluralism (11(2)) |
| Social/employment measures | Arts. 21, 23, 27–34 |
| Border, migration, security | Arts. 1, 4, 6, 18, 19, 24, 47 |
| Environmental and consumer measures | Arts. 37, 38 (principles — Art. 52(5) caveat) |
